review_notes: Read the whole target file plus Generic.lean (imported), Helpers.lean, Scanner.lean and If.lean. The file's single-step lemmas (rewind-left, halt→rewind) each inline the "write-back of the symbol under the head preserves tape cells" argument. That argument is already proved as `tape_readBackWrite_preserves` in the imported Generic.lean, and Scanner.lean uses it in one line. A second small repetition is the derivation `head = 0` from `read = Γ.start` plus no ▷ at positions ≥ 1. I did not compile the proposed rewrites. The rewrites rely on the goals having the `(t.writeAndMove (readBackWrite t.read).toΓ d).cells = t.cells` shape. Scanner.lean line 80 closes the same shape with `exact`, and the halt step needs only a `dsimp only [complementCfg]` defeq. The new `head_eq_zero_of_read_eq_start` lemma is a suggestion, not an existing declaration. Other possible repetition in the file (the head-minus-one block, the decides-in-time bookkeeping) is short or appears only once here, so I did not report it.

findings.problem: The same cell-preservation argument is proved inline in two proofs. The first is the cells goal of `complement_rewind_step_left` (lines 89–93). The second is the `¬ read = start` branch of the cells goal in `hstep1` inside `complementTM_rewind_and_flip` (lines 157–167). Both unfold `writeAndMove`, rewrite with `toΓ_readBackWrite_of_ne_start`, unfold `Tape.write`, split on `head = 0`, and close with `rfl` or `Function.update_eq_self`. This is exactly the statement of the already-imported lemma `tape_readBackWrite_preserves`, which Generic.lean proves with the identical script. The same script is also copied into If.lean (lines 242–246) and elsewhere. The halt step also re-derives `head = 0` from `read = Γ.start` and the no-▷ hypothesis (lines 160–162). `complement_rewind_step_base` does the same at lines 105–108.
findings.proposed_change:
Reuse the existing lemma in both places.

1. In `complement_rewind_step_left`, replace lines 89–93 with `· exact tape_readBackWrite_preserves c.output _ (Or.inr hread_ne)`. Scanner.lean line 80 closes the same goal shape this way.

2. In `hstep1`, replace the whole cells bullet (lines 157–167) with `· dsimp only [complementCfg]; exact tape_readBackWrite_preserves c_halt.output _ (by by_cases hread : c_halt.output.read = Γ.start; exacts [Or.inl (head_eq_zero_of_read_eq_start c_halt.output hread hnostart), Or.inr hread])`.

3. For the shared `head = 0` argument, add one small lemma. Statement: `theorem head_eq_zero_of_read_eq_start (t : Tape) (hread : t.read = Γ.start) (hns : ∀ j, j ≥ 1 → t.cells j ≠ Γ.start) : t.head = 0`. Proof: `by_contra h; exact hns t.head (by omega) hread`. `Tape.read` unfolds definitionally, so `hread` can be passed directly.

4. Use that lemma in `complement_rewind_step_base` (lines 105–108) and in `hstep1`. Ideally put it in Generic.lean next to `tape_readBackWrite_preserves`, so the other rewind-step proofs can use it too.
findings.benefit: Two copies of the unfold-split-update_eq_self argument shrink to one-line uses of a lemma that already exists and is tested. The `head = 0` argument is also stated once. Readers no longer have to re-check that the inline script matches the library lemma. Any change to `Tape.write` or `readBackWrite` then needs fixing in one place rather than in every copy, including those in other combinator files. Both rewritten proofs keep their actual hypotheses (`hread_ne`, `hnostart`) and need no new imports, since Generic.lean is already imported.

    (h : t.head = 0 ∨ t.read ≠ Γ.start) :
    (t.writeAndMove (readBackWrite t.read).toΓ d).cells = t.cells
